title: Follow up qa-v1-theory-733a556f906a5362f6b7ab7c
behavioral_concerns: follow up: Every handleSprintQA* method in qa_handlers.go follows an identical contract: nil h.qa ⇒ ErrWebUnavailable via handleQueryError; non-nil call to the underlying QA method; on error propagate via handleQueryError with boolean=true (API surface); on success writeSuccess(http.StatusOK, result, nil).

evidence.summary: qa_handlers.go (lines 10-201): 11 API handleSprintQA* methods follow identical nil-guard → call → handleQueryError(true,err) → writeSuccess(200) template; handleSprintQAPage (168-201) intentionally uses apiRoute=false + render() for HTML page routes. handleSprintQAIssues (51-72) is the only handler with extra limit-parse input validation that still preserves the contract.

handlers.go (lines 510-514, 652-673): HTML /projects/{p}/sprints/{s}/qa{,/shards/{x},/theories/{x}} routes dispatch handleSprintQAPage; /api/v1/projects/{p}/sprints/{s}/qa/* routes dispatch the 11 JSON handlers. handleQueryError (1056-1080) routes QAUseCaseError to writeQAError and ErrWebUnavailable to 503 'unavailable'.

qa_handlers_test.go covers TestQAQueryErrorsUseStablePublicCodes (qa.invalid_state envelope at 422 with code/category/guidance/correlation_id, no 'persistence' leakage) and TestQARoutesReturnBoundedJSONAndCompleteNoJavaScriptHTML (application/json Content-Type + schema_version=1 for API; 'Read-only QA', 'Conformance Review', <noscript> and no <script>alert for HTML). POST /api/.../qa returns 405. Note: the qaQueryFixture does not implement QAEvidenceQueries, so any QAEvidence/Adjudication/Issues/Issue/Assessment/SmokeSuite endpoint would exercise the !ok → ErrWebUnavailable → 503 path.

internal/app/sprint_usecases.go (lines 79-95) defines QAQueries (QAMap, QAStatus, QAShard, QATheory, QASynthesis) and additive QAEvidenceQueries (QAEvidence, QAAdjudication, QAIssues, QAIssue, QAAssessment, QASmokeSuite). The additive interface explains why some handlers use nil-check while others use comma-ok type assertion — both surface ErrWebUnavailable to handlers.go:1056-1080.

theories.claim: The `h.qa.(app.QAEvidenceQueries)` type-assertion guards used by handleSprintQAEvidence, handleSprintQAAdjudication, handleSprintQAIssues, handleSprintQAIssue, handleSprintQAAssessment, and handleSprintQASmokeSuite correctly surface ErrWebUnavailable when h.qa is nil, because Go's comma-ok type assertion on a nil interface returns (nil,false), causing the `if !ok { handleQueryError(w,r,true,app.ErrWebUnavailable); return }` branch to fire.
theories.basis: qa_handlers.go lines 24-28, 38-42, 52-56, 75-79, 89-93, 103-107 each use the same pattern: `queries, ok := h.qa.(app.QAEvidenceQueries); if !ok { h.handleQueryError(w, r, true, app.ErrWebUnavailable); return }`. Per the Go language spec, a comma-ok type assertion on a nil interface value yields the zero value of T and ok=false (no panic).
theories.verification_surface: internal/web/qa_handlers.go lines 24-28 (handleSprintQAEvidence), 38-42 (handleSprintQAAdjudication), 52-56 (handleSprintQAIssues), 75-79 (handleSprintQAIssue), 89-93 (handleSprintQAAssessment), 103-107 (handleSprintQASmokeSuite); internal/app/sprint_usecases.go lines 79-95 (QAQueries and QAEvidenceQueries interface definitions); internal/web/handlers.go lines 1056-1080 (handleQueryError mapping ErrWebUnavailable → 503 'unavailable').
theories.confirmation_condition: When h.qa is nil the six QAEvidenceQueries-gated handlers all return status 503 with code 'unavailable' via handleQueryError(w,r,true,ErrWebUnavailable).
theories.refutation_condition: Any of the six handlers either panics on nil h.qa, returns success, returns a status other than 503, or omits the apiRoute=true flag.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Cannot exercise the assertion dynamically via static reading alone; relies on Go language semantics for the comma-ok form.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Static inspection confirms identical if !ok guards across all six handlers; Go spec defines the comma-ok assertion behavior; the existing tests in qa_handlers_test.go do not cover the QAEvidenceQueries endpoints directly, but the contract is symmetric with the QAStatus endpoints that are tested.

theories.claim: All 11 JSON API handleSprintQA* methods in qa_handlers.go (lines 10-166) follow an identical 4-step contract: nil-guard h.qa → call underlying QA method → on error propagate via handleQueryError(w,r,true,err) → on success writeSuccess(http.StatusOK,result,nil). handleSprintQAPage (lines 168-201) intentionally diverges because it serves HTML page routes only (registered at handlers.go:510-514), not the /api/v1/.../qa routes.
theories.basis: Direct read of qa_handlers.go shows each of handleSprintQA (10-21), handleSprintQAEvidence (23-35), handleSprintQAAdjudication (37-49), handleSprintQAIssues (51-72), handleSprintQAIssue (74-86), handleSprintQAAssessment (88-100), handleSprintQASmokeSuite (102-114), handleSprintQAMap (116-127), handleSprintQAShard (129-140), handleSprintQATheory (142-153), handleSprintQASynthesis (155-166) gates nil h.qa → calls method → propagates error with apiRoute=true → writes success at 200. handlers.go:652-673 dispatches only the JSON handlers under /api/v1/projects/{p}/sprints/{s}/qa/*; handlers.go:510-514 dispatches handleSprintQAPage for /projects/{p}/sprints/{s}/qa{,/shards/{x},/theories/{x}}. handleQueryError (handlers.go:1056-1080) routes QAUseCaseError with apiRoute=true to writeQAError (status per qaErr.Code), and ErrWebUnavailable to status 503 / 'unavailable'.
theories.verification_surface: internal/web/qa_handlers.go lines 10-201; internal/web/handlers.go lines 510-514, 652-673, 1056-1080; internal/web/qa_handlers_test.go TestQAQueryErrorsUseStablePublicCodes (asserts qa.invalid_state at 422 with code/category/guidance/correlation_id) and TestQARoutesReturnBoundedJSONAndCompleteNoJavaScriptHTML (asserts JSON Content-Type and schema_version=1 for API routes, no <script> tags in HTML page routes).
theories.confirmation_condition: Each of the 11 API handlers matches the 4-step template with apiRoute=true on every error path and writeSuccess(http.StatusOK,result,nil) on success, and handleSprintQAPage is the sole HTML renderer with apiRoute=false.
theories.refutation_condition: Any JSON API handler omits the nil-guard, calls render() instead of writeSuccess, or passes apiRoute=false to handleQueryError; or any HTML page route (not handleSprintQAPage) is dispatched to a JSON-style handler.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Behavior cannot be exercised end-to-end without a running handler; only static reading is available.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only inspection of qa_handlers.go and handlers.go; cross-check against existing test coverage (TestQAQueryErrorsUseStablePublicCodes, TestQARoutesReturnBoundedJSONAndCompleteNoJavaScriptHTML) which already encode the contract's surface (error envelope at 422, JSON Content-Type, schema_version=1, noscript HTML).

theories.claim: handleSprintQAIssues is the only handleSprintQA* method that adds an extra input-validation step (parsing the `limit` query parameter) before delegating to the underlying QA method. The extra step propagates parse errors via handleQueryError(w,r,true,err), preserving the contract's intent (apiRoute=true on every error path) and uses writeSuccess(http.StatusOK,result,nil) on success, so it is a faithful extension rather than a deviation.
theories.basis: qa_handlers.go lines 57-65 introduce `if value := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); value != "" { parsed, err := strconv.Atoi(value); if err != nil { h.handleQueryError(w, r, true, err); return }; limit = parsed }` between the QAEvidenceQueries guard and the underlying queries.QAIssues call. The success path (line 71) still calls writeSuccess(w, r, http.StatusOK, result, nil).
theories.confirmation_condition: The limit-parse error path passes apiRoute=true to handleQueryError and the success path uses writeSuccess(http.StatusOK,result,nil) like every other handler.
theories.refutation_condition: handleSprintQAIssues uses apiRoute=false for the parse error, omits the nil-guard, or skips writeSuccess on success.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Static read of qa_handlers.go:51-72 confirms the structure.
